thread:
anya: Heads-up — after the canary we're seeing a small but repeatable mismatch in telemetry between the kernel selector and the SM probe on L4 nodes. Appears when sequence length > 1024 and KV cache warmup occurs.

sam: Ugh. Is this the probe deciding 'no SM feature' then later runtime using the optimized H100/A100 path by mistake? :confused:

anya: Exactly — probe says 'no advanced simd' for some tiles, selector falls back, but the runtime still picks the optimized kernel later in the pipeline. Logs show `selected_kernel=attn_opt_v2` but `sm_flags=~SIMD_AVX` for the device.

olga: Can you paste the minimal log snippet? Might be a race between device capability caching and the probe refresh.

anya: Sure — snippet: ```2026-02-11T15:14:02Z probe: sm_probe_result: lanes=32 simd=false tile_mask=0x1f``` ```2026-02-11T15:14:03Z selector: selected_kernel=attn_opt_v2 heuristic_score=0.82``` ```2026-02-11T15:14:04Z runtime: load_kv_cache hits=128 latency_ms=1.8```

luis: Hmm looks like probe result TTL/expiry is long and there's a background poll that can update feature flags after selector runs. If selector caches device->kernel mapping per-request, it may read stale flags.

sam: Two obvious fixes: 1) move gating earlier so selector consults the authoritative device flags at decision time, or 2) make probe updates atomic relative to selector reads (rwlock). Tradeoffs?

olga: 1) adds latency to selection path — per-request device read could be costly, but we already have a device-capability cache. 2) rwlock increases complexity and possible contention during mass probe refresh.

anya: Another option: versioned capability tokens. Probe writes new token when capabilities change; selector checks token id cheaply and only rereads full flags when id differs. Low overhead on hot path.

luis: I like token approach. Similar to a generation counter — selector can compare `cap_gen` attached to device struct. Very cheap. If mismatch -> full read + validate fallback.

sam: Implementation note: ensure `cap_gen` increment is monotonic across restarts and persisted for private deployments? Not necessary persisted, just per-process monotonic.

olga: Also need to audit where `selected_kernel` can be overridden later. Looks like there is a post-selection autotune pass that may swap kernels based on microbench signals. That pass must respect cap_gen — otherwise it might pick a kernel that requires features we probed as absent.

anya: Good catch. I'll open a small follow-up RFC for: (a) cap_gen token on device struct, (b) selector check inline, (c) autotune pass to validate kernel feature requirements against current cap snapshot.

sam: Can we add a cheap assertion in CI: for every device/probe pair in the integration matrix, ensure selector never picks a kernel that requires flags absent in the latest probe? Fails fast in dev.

luis: Yeah add integration test + a fuzz harness that simulates delayed probe updates. We already have the test infra in eng-runtime.

anya: Action items: anya -> RFC draft by EOD tomorrow; sam -> add CI assertion ticket; luis -> prototype cap_gen patches on device struct and node-local probe; olga -> audit autotune override code for cap checks.

dev-bot: Deploy-bot: canary rollout 0.9.7 -> staging started (canary group: l4-us-west-2). Monitoring channels: eng-runtime, incidents.

sam: Thanks — I'll pause the rest of the canary until we have the token guard in place. :thumbsup:

anya: Thx all. Keeping this thread for progress updates.
